(a) Effective Date Modification.—
        (1) In general.—Paragraph (2) of section 903(d) of the American Jobs Creation Act of 2004 is amended to read as follows:“(2) Exception for reportable or listed transactions.—“(A) In general.—The amendments made by subsection (c) shall apply with respect to interest accruing after October 3, 2004.“(B) Special rule for certain listed and reportable transactions.—“(i) In general.—Except as provided in clauses (ii), (iii), and (iv), the amendments made by subsection (c) shall also apply with respect to interest accruing on or before October 3, 2004.“(ii) Participants in settlement initiatives.—Clause (i) shall not apply to any transaction if, as of January 23, 2006—“(I) the taxpayer is participating in a settlement initiative described in Internal Revenue Service Announcement 2005–80 with respect to such transaction, or“(II) the taxpayer has entered into a settlement agreement pursuant to such an initiative.Subclause (I) shall not apply to any taxpayer if, after January 23, 2006, the taxpayer withdraws from, or terminates, participation in the initiative or the Secretary of the Treasury or the Secretary’s delegate determines that a settlement agreement will not be reached pursuant to the initiative within a reasonable period of time.“(iii) Taxpayers acting in good faith.—The Secretary of the Treasury may except from the application of clause (i) any transaction in which the taxpayer has acted reasonably and in good faith.“(iv) Closed transactions.—Clause (i) shall not apply to a transaction if, as of December 14, 2005—“(I) the assessment of all Federal income taxes for the taxable year in which the tax liability to which the interest relates arose is prevented by the operation of any law or rule of law, or“(II) a closing agreement under section 7121 has been entered into with respect to the tax liability arising in connection with the transaction.”. 
        (2) Effective date.—The amendment made by this subsection shall take effect as if included in the provisions of the American Jobs Creation Act of 2004 to which it relates.  
    (b) Treatment of Amended Returns and Other Similar Notices of Additional Tax Owed.—
        (1) In general.—Section 6404(g)(1) (relating to suspension) is amended by adding at the end the following new sentence: “If, after the return for a taxable year is filed, the taxpayer provides to the Secretary 1 or more signed written documents showing that the taxpayer owes an additional amount of tax for the taxable year, clause (i) shall be applied by substituting the date the last of the documents was provided for the date on which the return is filed.”. 
        (2) Effective date.—The amendment made by this subsection shall apply to documents provided on or after the date of the enactment of this Act.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that "participating in a settlement initiative" and "settlement agreement" signal participation, but these refer to a taxpayer resolving its own tax liability, not outside parties being consulted on a federal policy decision. The section only modifies effective dates and interest-suspension rules for tax transactions. It contains no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside entities, rulemaking mandate, or grant of a right to sue.
fable.s: the taxpayer is participating in a settlement initiative described in Internal Revenue Service Announcement 2005–80 with respect to such transaction

qwen_block.w: The section discusses tax liability and interest calculations based on whether a taxpayer is participating in a settlement initiative or has entered into a settlement agreement. This is an administrative or legal status regarding tax compliance and enforcement, not a process where the government consults with outside parties to make a policy decision. The 'participation' mentioned refers to the taxpayer's involvement in a pre-existing IRS settlement program, which is akin to applying for a specific tax treatment or resolving a dispute, not participating in the formulation of government decisions.
qwen_block.s: the taxpayer is participating in a settlement initiative described in Internal Revenue Service Announcement 2005–80 with respect to such transaction

opus.w: Here "participating" means a taxpayer joining an IRS settlement program to resolve their own tax liability. That is an individual enforcement or settlement matter, not outsiders being consulted before a federal policy decision. The section only changes effective dates and rules for suspending interest. It does not require or authorize rulemaking, public comment, hearings, advisory bodies, consultation with outside entities, or a new right to sue, so matching the keyword is not enough.
opus.s: the taxpayer is participating in a settlement initiative described in Internal Revenue Service Announcement 2005–80 with respect to such transaction, or“(II) the taxpayer has entered into a settlement agreement pursuant to such an initiative.
opus.b:
1. **Tempting reading and why it fails:** The section uses the words "participating in a settlement initiative," "settlement agreement," and "closing agreement," which could look like outside parties (taxpayers) taking part in a federal decision. That reading doesn't hold. These are individual taxpayers settling or closing their own tax liabilities with the IRS, which is closer to resolving an enforcement matter or an application than to taking part in a federal policy decision. The section has no comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking authority, outside consultation, or new right to sue. The amended-return rule also just covers a taxpayer giving the Secretary documents about tax owed.

qwen_chat.w: The section describes the effective dates of tax amendments and the treatment of amended returns. While it mentions taxpayers 'participating' in settlement initiatives, this refers to the taxpayer's voluntary engagement in an existing administrative process, not a statutory requirement for the federal government to consult with outside parties before making a decision. The interactions are between taxpayers and the IRS (a federal agency), which does not constitute participation as defined (consultation with non-federal entities before a decision).
qwen_chat.s: the taxpayer is participating in a settlement initiative described in Internal Revenue Service Announcement 2005–80 with respect to such transaction
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: The text mentions taxpayers "participating in a settlement initiative" or "entering into a settlement agreement," which might suggest participation. However, this is a procedural description of how existing tax laws apply to specific transactions (reportable/listed transactions) and defines the effective dates of interest accrual. It does not establish a new process for the government to consult with the public or outside entities before making a policy decision. The "participation" here is the taxpayer's voluntary action in a pre-existing administrative process, not a statutory requirement for the government to seek input from outsiders. Furthermore, the interaction described is between the taxpayer and the IRS (an internal federal agency), which falls under intra-governmental or administrative enforcement, not the defined "participation" of consulting with outside parties before a decision.
